approach: Two root causes, fixed in place. (1) The email allow-list scan ran only in admit(), after the candidate was built, so the producer got no feedback and the refusal named a file but no line. Fix: a line-numbered scan of the snapshot's working diff (athena-gate content.rs, reusing disallowed_emails and the configured PersonalData), wrapped in admission.rs and called from produce_and_verify in run/mod.rs between producer_loop and candidate_stage, with the helper in run/candidate.rs. A finding closes the job as failure('admission refused the change: <path>:<line> adds an email address outside the allow-list'). Admission keeps its own scan as the backstop. (2) Earlier-case search: narrow_cases takes only CaseRows with the same class_of_work and category, newest 5 first, and never reads the outcome's refusal reason. Three conditions each leave 4nff with no earlier cases: (a) the earlier jobs' cases differ in class_of_work or category; (b) five or more newer unrelated cases in the busy 'code'/'failed' bucket crowd the older refusals out of the cap; (c) 9e8t and akwq have no CaseRow. In each, the model sees none and picks 'new', and apply_answer drops any case not passed in and in the chosen class, so the record shows new_class=true and empty earlier_cases. records/ is absent from my copy, so which condition occurred is not proven; the fix covers all three. Event gains the job's outcome reason; Records gains job_reasons (job id to outcome reason) filled by read_records; narrow_cases lists first the cases whose job's outcome has the same admission refusal key as the event, then the class/category matches, capped at CASE_CAP. For a matching job with no CaseRow there is no case to cite, so introspect() adds a flag naming those jobs. apply_answer is unchanged. Add the one producer.md line and a CHANGELOG entry naming both root causes. docs/system-facts.md is NOT touched (answer to finding 3): the budgets test compares the facts file with the producer row, which is the maximum across capabilities, and the study capability's producer set (read: crates/athena-cap-study/prompts/producer.md) is the largest at 1257; the change set has about 146 tokens free per the brief, so a line of about 30 tokens leaves the row at 1257 and the planner row does not use producer.md.

decisions.choice: Run the scan in produce_and_verify (run/mod.rs), right after producer_loop returns and before candidate_stage; the helper working_diff_scan lives in run/candidate.rs. It is a hard stop (Flow::Stop with a failure reason), not a send-back.
decisions.reason: The request says a disallowed address fails the producer's own run and names file and line. This placement keeps producer.rs, which is not a listed deliverable, untouched. It runs before any candidate commit is built and before any 'candidate' UI line. The reason keeps the 'admission refused the change: ' prefix, so introspection's matcher sees the same text as an admission refusal. Trade-off: it runs once on the final work tree, not on each send-back pass.

decisions.choice: Add disallowed_email_lines in athena-gate content.rs: run `git diff -U0 --no-color --no-renames --no-ext-diff <from> <to>` through Git::run_bytes, parse the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` headers to number added lines, and call the existing disallowed_emails on each. admission.rs wraps it as working_diff_email_violations.
decisions.reason: Git::added_lines returns (path, line text) with no line numbers, and the failure must name the line. Counting only added lines keeps an address already in the base from being blamed on the producer. The same disallowed_emails and PersonalData mean one email rule and one allow-list (buy-first).

decisions.choice: No retry-seed work: an in-loop failure starts the retry fresh from the base, with the path:line reason in the failure record. The test asserts the job closes Failed, not TimedOut.
decisions.reason: tree_seed needs a rejected candidate that qualifies_for_tree_retry and resume_seed needs a resume mark written only after the candidate is built, so an admission-refused job gets neither seed today either. Nothing is lost relative to a refused candidate.

rejected.option: Keep the work tree like keep_timed_out_work

decisions.reason: event.what is composed from title, reason and failure details, so splitting it can pull in unrelated text. Event.reason does not depend on the job's own outcome being on disk in the tree read_records walks.

rejected.why: Depends on the job's own outcome being on disk in the walked tree; not confirmed.

decisions.choice: narrow_cases order: first cases whose job's outcome has a refusal key equal to the event's key (newest first), then class_of_work+category matches (newest first), de-duplicated by id, truncated to CASE_CAP. refusal_keys(reason) in admission.rs returns [] unless the reason starts with REFUSED_PREFIX; it splits the rest on '; ' and drops a leading path-like token (containing '.', '/' or ':') from each segment. Admission owns REFUSED_PREFIX and the email rule constant EMAIL_RULE; admit(), the in-loop scan and the matcher use them.
decisions.reason: Refusal matches go first so same-reason cases cannot be crowded out of the cap (cause b); matching across class_of_work and category covers cause (a). Ignoring the file name lets refusals naming different files match, as 9e8t and akwq's did. The key is general to admission rules, as the request says 'the admission refusal reason'.

rejected.why: It would not cover other admission refusals.

decisions.reason: If 9e8t and akwq were never introspected, no introspection id exists to cite, and new_class=true for 4nff is then correct. The flag makes the repeat visible instead of silent.

risks.risk: Hunk-header parsing mis-numbers lines (zero-add hunks, binary files, odd path characters).
risks.mitigation: Parse only `+c[,d]` of the `@@` header and count only lines starting '+' (not '+++'); skip `+++ /dev/null`; tests for added, modified (two hunks) and deleted files. An unparsable hunk gives no finding, and admission still catches the address.

risks.risk: The refusal key matches unrelated refusals, or refusal matches fill the cap and hide class/category cases.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in introspect.rs's tests module, in-memory data plus one tempdir read. Records is built from Records::default() plus CaseRow, ClassRow and job_reasons values: two older cases in one registered class whose jobs' outcome reasons are 'admission refused the change: <path A> adds an email address outside the allow-list' and '... <path B> ...', same class_of_work ('code') and category ('failed') as the event; six newer unrelated cases in the same bucket (cause b); a third refusal case with a different class_of_work (cause a); a third job with the same refusal but no CaseRow (cause c). The event carries reason '... <path C>:<line> adds an email address outside the allow-list'. A separate part writes two outcome files into a tempdir (AnyRecord::Outcome via canonical_path) and asserts read_records fills job_reasons. Then it asserts narrow_cases returns the refusal-matched cases first (both same-bucket cases and the different-class case), capped at CASE_CAP, unrelated cases do not displace them, an event with a different refusal pulls none, and unrecorded_matches returns the uncased job. It passes the narrowed ids to Athena::apply_answer with an Answer that picks the existing class and cites both.
demonstrations.observes: The narrowed list holds both refusal cases first; the record has non-empty earlier_cases (both ids), new_class false and dropped_ids empty.
demonstrations.fails_without: On base narrow_cases returns the five newest unrelated same-bucket cases, so neither refusal case is passed in and apply_answer would drop both into dropped_ids. The test also uses the new fields Records.job_reasons and Event.reason, so on base it fails to compile; that is unavoidable because the matcher needs the outcome reason, which base never reads. The crowding assertion states the behavioral gap.

open_questions: records/ is absent from my copy, so I could not read introspection 20261025-074235-4nff or the outcomes of 9e8t and akwq. The scan runs once after the producer loop ends, not on each send-back pass; a per-pass check needs a producer.rs change outside the listed deliverables.
